news.title: 'It was the right decision!' - Carlo Ancelotti defends Neymar World Cup call-up as Brazil legend officially retires from international football
news.lede: Brazil head coach Carlo Ancelotti has broken his silence on Neymar’s retirement from international football, staunchly defending his choice to include the veteran in his 2026 World Cup squad. The Italian tactician admitted the superstar’s physical preparation was a source of frustration but insisted his presence was vital for the Selecao. Neymar has officially brought the curtain down on his illustrious 16-year international career. The 34-year-old’s decision comes in the wake of a painful World Cup round of 16 elimination against Norway.

news.title: ‘Selling the soul of football’?: The financial and sporting impact of Fifa’s US$20bn plan to sell the World Cup and change soccer forever
news.lede: Gianni Infantino was elected as Fifa president a decade ago, promising to restore Fifa’s reputation following the allegations of corruption that ultimately ended the reign of his predecessor Sepp Blatter. During that time, Fifa and Infantino have displayed a seemingly insatiable appetite for growth, whether it’s creating new tournaments, cozying up to wealthy or influential regimes, or expanding and aggressively monetising its grand cash cow – the men’s World Cup. Having initially projected revenues of US$11 billion, world soccer’s governing body has told member associations it has generated as much as US$15 billion. But it has no desire to stop there.

news.title: Why Germany may stand up against FIFA's World Cup sell off
news.lede: Leading figures in German football have lined up to criticize Gianni Infantino’s plans to sell a stake in the World Cup. Germany is showing signs that they may ready to oppose Infantino's re-election. "We must not let it become a pawn in the hands of investors. We must not lose the fans' support, but we are well on our way to squandering that support.

news.title: A former World Cup player launches the idea of obtaining one million signatures for Messi to play in the 2030 World Cup
news.lede: The future of Lionel Messi with the Argentina National Team continues to be the center of debate across the football world. Following the Rosario star's recent performances on the major international stage, the repercussions have continued to multiply throughout the continent. On this occasion, the statements came from Bolivia through an interview granted to the program Super Deportivo Radio, a conversation that was quickly echoed by diario Olé and various international media outlets due to the emotional weight of his words. The one who spoke up was Marco Antonio "El Diablo" Etcheverry, a legendary former Bolivia national team footballer who played in the 1994 United States World Cup.

news.title: Infantino wants to sell the World Cup. Can anyone stop him?
news.lede: Fifa members who vote through Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell the World Cup to investors will get $40m. Vote it down, and it’s just $10m. Here, chief sports writer Lawrence Ostlere dissects the pitch football can’t refuse – and how Uefa and players are readying themselves to push back – in this week's Inside Football newsletter. Infantino sent a letter to Fifa’s 211 member associations this week, which The Independent has seen, pitching his big idea to sell stakes in the World Cup to investors.

news.title: Fifa ‘undermining the very foundations of football’, says AFC as Uefa talks loom
news.lede: Asian Football Confederation may hold balance of power. Uefa to hold emergency meeting on Thursday. The Asian Football Confederation has accused Fifa of undermining the foundations of football by failing to consult the confederations over their plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors. In a letter sent on Thursday by president Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa to AFC’s 47 members, which has been seen by the Guardian, Fifa’s unilateral actions in doing a deal with Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Capital to buy 20% of a new company that would control the commercial rights of all global tournaments is roundly condemned.

news.title: UEFA set for emergency meeting on FIFA World Cup proposal
news.lede: UEFA is reportedly soon to hold an emergency meeting to discuss FIFA's plans to effectively sell off a stake in the World Cup. European football's governing body has expressed stiff opposition to the plan. Several media outlets reported on Thursday that UEFA had called an afternoon meeting of its 55 members to discuss a response to FIFA's plans to create a new commercial subsidiary valued at $20 billion (roughly €17.5 billion) and sell a non-controlling minority stake of it to investors. UEFA, European football's governing body, came out publicly in opposition to the plan within an hour of it first being reported by the Financial Times and Times on Monday.
